title: Provision-to-ready CLI (rw-fleet) — Operator UX feedback + prioritized fixes
content:
Context
- This doc captures feedback from Infra/SRE operators using the new provisioning CLI during staging pilot + 1 customer expansion dry-run.
- Source: ad-hoc notes during pilot, #eng-infra thread (1709738000), and 1:1s with oncall/SRE.
- Target CLI shape (current): `rw-fleet` (aka “fleetctl” in some notes). Commands include:
  - `rw-fleet provision run ...`
  - `rw-fleet provision status ...`
  - `rw-fleet provision rerun-stage ...`
  - `rw-fleet provision pause/resume ...`
  - `--dry-run` supported on run + rerun-stage

Overall themes (what’s hurting time-to-ready)
1) Discoverability: operators can’t tell what inputs are required until after a failed attempt.
2) Error messages are too “internal”: they surface service/queue errors instead of actionable next steps.
3) Context switching: CLI outputs don’t include direct links (logs/dashboards/runbook/Linear) so operators bounce between tools.
4) Stage semantics confusion: “bootstrap” vs “validate” vs “ready” isn’t obvious from CLI status.
5) Safe retries: fear of making it worse; rerun-stage needs stronger guardrails and clearer idempotency messaging.

Current command usage patterns observed
- Most common action is “start a run” + “check status repeatedly”. Operators want the status to be self-contained.
- Rerun-stage used mostly for:
  - Imaging timeouts
  - Helm/bootstrap misconfig
  - Validation failures (GPU health, DNS/TLS)
- Pause/resume used to hold capacity out of routing during investigation.

Top pain points + missing features (raw notes)

A. `provision run` UX
- Missing: a single “pool selector” story.
  - Today: some commands want `--pool-id`, others accept `--customer` + `--region` + `--sku` but not consistently.
  - Operator expectation: “I know the pool name (human) and env; let me target it.”
- `--help` output is noisy and doesn’t show examples.
  - Request: include 2–3 copy-paste examples for common flows: new pool, expansion, rerun validation.
- Required flags aren’t enforced early.
  - Example failure: command starts, then the service rejects after 20s: “missing field: pool_config.runtime_chart_version”. Operators want immediate validation.
- `--dry-run` output is not useful.
  - Current dry-run prints a blob of JSON (internal request payload) w/ fields operators don’t understand.
  - Want: explicit checklist: “will create/modify resources: X, will apply image: Y, will run canary: yes/no” and which stages will execute.

B. `status` UX
- The status output doesn’t answer the first operator question: “Is it stuck? If yes, what should I do now?”
- Missing stage timing context.
  - Operators asked for: elapsed time per stage, plus stage budget (“expected 10–25m; currently 47m”).
- Missing correlation IDs / links.
  - When status shows “Failed”, there’s no direct link to:
    - provisioning run logs (control plane)
    - terraform apply logs
    - perf-canary summary JSON
    - readiness dashboard filtered by pool/run
- Some statuses are misleading:
  - “Bootstrapping” includes multiple sub-steps (helm install, node labeling, runtime registration). Operators want at least 2 sub-statuses or “latest event” line.

C. Rerun + pause/resume semantics
- Rerun-stage warns are too generic (“rerunning may be unsafe”). Operators want it to be specific:
  - “Safe to rerun: validation, perf-canary”
  - “Potentially destructive: imaging, terraform apply”
- Need a “confirm you understand” prompt or `--yes` for destructive-ish stages.
- Want “rerun from last failed stage” shortcut.
  - Today: operator has to find the stage name and retype it.
- Pause/resume doesn’t describe what’s paused.
  - Does pause stop retries? stop state transitions? just stop routing readiness? The behavior needs to be printed.

D. Errors / messaging
- Too many errors are raw.
  - Examples reported:
    - “rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to upsert run record”
    - “helm upgrade failed: context deadline exceeded” (without which chart/release/namespace)
    - “x509: certificate signed by unknown authority” (without clarifying which endpoint or how to validate trust chain)
- Need consistent error categories.
  - Operators want errors grouped like: QUOTA, IAM, NETWORKING, GPU_HEALTH, HELM/BOOTSTRAP, CONFIG_VALIDATION, PERF_CANARY.
- Need explicit recommended next step.
  - Example: if QUOTA -> show link to quota runbook section + suggestion to re-run terraform apply after quota resolved.

E. Output formatting
- Status output is hard to scan.
  - Request: a one-line summary + indented stage list + last event.
  - Request: always show pool identifiers at top (pool-id, pool name, customer, region, sku, env).
- Prefer stable text output for copying into Slack threads.
  - `--json` is fine, but default should be “human readable + copyable”.

Prioritized fixes (proposal)

P0 (do these before next pilot / to reduce oncall load)
1) Make `status` actionable (links + next step)
  - Add fields to default output:
    - Run ID, Pool ID, customer, env, region, SKU
    - Correlation ID
    - Stage list with elapsed time, and “budget” line
    - Last failure summary with error category
    - Links:
      - Dedicated readiness dashboard (filtered)
      - Run logs (control plane)
      - Terraform apply log artifact
      - Perf-canary summary (if available)
      - Runbook anchor link
  - Acceptance: operator can paste `rw-fleet provision status ...` into #eng-infra and it contains everything needed to start triage.

2) Harden required-flag + early validation for `provision run`
  - CLI should validate:
    - required flags present
    - flag combinations coherent (mutually exclusive)
    - config schema validation runs locally first (same rules as server) when possible
  - Print a clear “Inputs resolved to:” section before execution.

3) Safer rerun semantics
  - Add `rw-fleet provision rerun-last-failed --run-id ...`.
  - Add stage safety labeling + required `--yes` for terraform/imaging reruns.
  - On rerun, print “what will be reused” (cached artifacts) vs “what will be recreated”.

4) Error message improvements for top 5 failure modes
  - QUOTA (terraform apply)
  - IAM missing permission (staging)
  - DNS/TLS misconfig (validation)
  - GPU health/ECC (validation)
  - Helm values misconfig (bootstrapping)
  - Format: one-line summary + category + top 3 debug commands + runbook link.

P1 (next iteration; improves speed but not strictly blocking)
5) `--follow` mode for status
  - `rw-fleet provision status --run-id ... --follow` prints updates as events arrive.
  - Also useful: `--watch 10s` if follow is harder.

6) Better `--dry-run`
  - Print an execution plan similar to terraform:
    - stages to execute
    - resources to create/modify (high-level)
    - image version + runtime/chart version
    - estimated time-to-ready range (based on region/SKU historical baseline)

7) Pool selector consistency
  - Standardize on one of:
    - `--pool-id` everywhere, plus `rw-fleet pools list/find` helper
    - OR: allow `--pool <customer>/<env>/<region>/<pool-name>` everywhere
  - At minimum, make `--pool-id` accepted for all commands.

8) `--json` output contract
  - Operators building tooling want a stable JSON schema for status.
  - Add `--json` and version it (e.g., `cli_output_version=1`).

P2 (quality-of-life)
9) Add “copy links” shortcuts
  - `rw-fleet provision links --run-id ...` prints only URLs.

10) Shell completion
  - Autocomplete stage names, regions, common flags.

11) Inline glossary
  - `rw-fleet provision explain bootstrapping` prints what happens + what success looks like.

Suggested default output (example)

Command:
  rw-fleet provision status --run-id prun_01HRV... 

Output (proposed):
  Run: prun_01HRV... (env=staging)
  Pool: pool_8f3c... name=acme-search-dedicated-01 customer=acme region=us-east-1 sku=h100x8
  State: BOOTSTRAPPING (elapsed 01:12:33)  last_event=helm_release_apply

  Stages:
    - Requested      00:00:00
    - Provisioning   00:14:22 (budget p95 00:25:00)
    - Imaging        00:22:18 (budget p95 00:35:00)
    - Bootstrapping  00:35:53 (budget p95 00:20:00)  <- over budget
    - Validating     pending
    - Ready          pending

  Latest failure:
    Category: HELM_BOOTSTRAP
    Summary: Helm upgrade timed out (release=redwood-runtime, ns=fleet-system)
    Next steps:
      1) Check helm events: kubectl -n fleet-system describe pod -l app=redwood-runtime
      2) Check values diff: rw-fleet provision debug helm-values --run-id ...
      3) If values misconfig, fix config and rerun: rw-fleet provision rerun-stage --run-id ... --stage bootstrapping --yes

  Links:
    - Dashboard: https://observability.redwood.ai/d/dedicated-readiness?pool_id=pool_8f3c...&run_id=prun_01HRV...
    - Control plane logs: https://console.redwood.ai/fleet/runs/prun_01HRV...
    - Terraform logs: s3://redwood-provisioning-logs/staging/prun_01HRV.../terraform.log
    - Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/.../dedicated-pool-provisioning-runbook#bootstrapping

Open questions / decisions needed
- Should the CLI be “operator-only” (internal auth) or also used by Solutions Eng / CS? If the latter, we need safer defaults and less internal jargon.
- Do we want a “guided mode” (interactive prompts) or keep everything flags-only? (Operators split 50/50.)
- Where do we host log links so they work for everyone (S3 vs console deep links)?

Owner notes / next steps
- Vanessa + Gabe: please map P0 items to a single tracking issue (or update ENG-2750 checklist) so we can close the loop with operators.
- Rafael: sanity-check error categories against SRE alert taxonomy (so CLI output matches paging/tickets).
- Victor: DNS/TLS troubleshooting snippet would be good to embed in the CLI for NETWORKING category (short + consistent).

Appendix: verbatim operator quotes (anonymized-ish)
- “I don’t know what to do with ‘rpc Unknown’. Tell me if it’s safe to rerun or if I need to page someone.”
- “Status is missing the one thing I want: the dashboard link filtered to the pool/run.”
- “Rerun-stage makes me nervous. I want it to say ‘this is idempotent’ or ‘this will recreate nodes’.”
- “Dry-run should tell me what versions I’m about to deploy (image/runtime/chart).”
